facts.label: Liquidity and maturity profile

facts.label: Data quality and definitions
facts.text: Three definitions shape every ratio in this report. EBITDA is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization because the filings print none; debt is balance-sheet carrying value, USD 2.566 million below principal at 30 September 2026; and interest cover uses cash interest paid, which is uneven by quarter because the notes pay on 1 May and 1 November. Fourth-quarter 2025 is derived, not reported, and the 2025 annual report recast the 2024 and 2023 expense lines between functions without changing totals. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a moderate, steady view is the pace of shareholder returns: buybacks took 76.39% of nine-month free cash flow, USD 100.2 million of the programme remains and USD 305.0 million of the revolving loan is undrawn, so management could fund further repurchases or the DealerClub earnout with debt, with no sponsor involved. The view would worsen if repurchases were funded by revolver borrowings, if the earnout were paid in cash or if the audience decline reached Dealer revenue; it would improve if repurchases slowed in favour of repayment or the notes were refinanced early. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that earnings, cash flow and the balance sheet have moved the right way together: leverage fell from 2.97x to 2.73x, free cash flow stayed steady and USD 305.0 million of the revolving loan is undrawn, while management attributes the audience decline to a deliberate shift towards high-intent shoppers and revenue per dealer rose 3%. If that account holds, the 2026 cost savings are a lasting margin gain and the 2028 notes can be refinanced from a lower leverage base. The strongest evidence against a comfortable reading is that debt is valued at 96.02% of principal against 99.80% at the end of 2025, with flat revenue and month-to-month dealer subscriptions behind it. The view would improve if dealer customers and revenue per dealer rose together for two quarters while repurchases slowed in favour of repayment or the notes were refinanced early, and it would worsen if EBITDA fell back to its FY2025 level, which would take leverage to 2.91x, if repurchases were funded from the revolving loan or if dealer customers fell by more than the 1% seen now. Basis: calculation LV1; calculation LV3; calculation DS2; calculation FV1; calculation FV2; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21

facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is high and the contest is for audience: the direct competitors named are CarGurus, AutoTrader and TrueCar, dealer software providers such as Cox Automotive compete for dealer budgets, and search engines, social platforms and generative AI chat engines compete for the same shoppers. Substitutes matter most through AI answer engines that can give vehicle information without sending shoppers to Cars.com, which would cut organic traffic and the value of a dealer subscription. Dealer buyer power is limited because no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, but OEM and National customers are few and can change media strategy independent of the product, which explains the volatility of that line. Search engines and app stores hold the most supplier power because most traffic arrives organically and ranking changes can lower visits. facts.text: Scale and market position are average: the issuer describes industry-leading brand recognition, but revenue of USD 725.943 million over the last twelve months cannot be ranked because no market share or peer data are supplied. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The most plausible downside is audience-led. Search and AI platforms divert organic traffic and unique visitors keep falling beyond the 10% seen in nine months 2026; the first operational break is at the dealer, where higher-tier package adoption stalls, dealer customers fall faster than the 1% now seen and Dealer revenue, 90.36% of the total, stops growing while OEM and National revenue keeps falling. With the March 2026 cost reduction already taken, little cost cushion is left, so EBITDA drifts back towards its FY2025 level, 6.13% below the last twelve months. At that level carrying-value debt is 2.91x EBITDA, net debt 2.48x and cash interest cover 5.33x, so the transmission is moderate leverage rising from 2.73x and not a covenant event. Liquidity holds: free cash flow at the FY2025 level of USD 125.734 million still funds interest and capital expenditure, and USD 305.0 million of the revolving loan is undrawn. The pressure arrives at refinancing: even if all free cash flow and cash were kept for the 25 months to October 2028, USD 67.641 million of the USD 400.0 million notes would still need other funding, and any repurchases add to that gap. Management's levers are to suspend the repurchase programme, cut costs again, settle the DealerClub earnout in stock where agreed or draw the revolving loan. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; whether the notes can be refinanced on acceptable terms against a weaker audience is the open question, and the signals to watch are in the monitoring triggers. Basis: calculation DS1; calculation DS2; calculation DS3; calculation DS4; calculation RP1; calculation FC1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 26

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Cars.com presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring dealer subscriptions, low customer concentration and small capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking audience, a cost-led earnings recovery and a shareholder-first financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow has been steady across three periods and converts 79.34% of EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA holding near its current level, the revolving loan staying available and repurchases slowing before the November 2028 maturity. The primary downside path is audience erosion that reaches Dealer revenue. A more definitive opinion would require the credit agreement and indenture, the proxy statement, the issuer's reconciliation of EBITDA, and peer and market-price data. ## Findings
### Bottom line

spans.text: # Cars.com Inc. (cars-1683606): financial foundation
## Request

Financial foundation for Cars.com Inc. (cars-1683606), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the five supplied annual and quarterly filings, in US dollars.
## Sources

| Module | Name | sha256 | Use |

| CP-0 | Source readiness | 17142d795f3e64b9aaae6cf2d6803983ede07492de5804d8adc07b81886738ad | Source inventory, readiness limits, document dates, financing documents named but not supplied, and the sources searched for letters of credit and lender-defined EBITDA. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage is moderate and improving, and nothing falls due before November 2028: carrying-value debt is 2.73x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026, down from 2.97x at year-end 2025, with interest covered 5.67x. Creditors therefore depend mainly on holding earnings through the 2028 refinancing of the USD 400.0 million notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9, 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation RT4; calculation RT13; calculation RT15

Reported EBITDA is calculated, not issuer-stated, and the issuer's own Total Net Leverage Ratio of 1.77x is lower than the 2.33x net leverage calculated here because the credit-agreement definitions are not supplied. Free cash flow converts 79.34% of EBITDA, but share repurchases absorbed 76.39% of nine-month free cash flow, so further deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth more than on debt repayment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 26; calculation RT14; calculation FC2; calculation FC3
### Leverage and coverage

Last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose 6.53% from USD 152.092 million in FY2025 to USD 162.020 million to 30 September 2026, while carrying-value debt fell 2.01%, so most of the move in leverage from 2.97x to 2.73x comes from earnings and not from repayment. Over the first nine months of 2026 EBITDA rose USD 9.928 million, of which revenue added USD 2.704 million and lower cash operating costs USD 7.224 million, after a USD 8.5 million workforce-reduction expense in the first quarter. The gain is therefore cost-led on flat revenue, which makes it more exposed to reversal than a revenue-led gain would be.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 9, 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; calculation EG1; calculation DG1; calculation EG2; calculation RT4; calculation RT13

Interest cover on cash interest paid has risen at every date shown, from 4.94x in FY2024 and 5.08x in FY2025 to 5.67x, as last-twelve-months cash interest paid fell to USD 28.553 million while EBITDA rose. The coupon on the notes alone costs USD 25.5 million a year, so cover is mostly a function of EBITDA and not of the revolving loan rate.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation RT3; calculation RT6; calculation RT15; calculation LI3; calculation CP1

The strongest contrary evidence is a flat top line and a shrinking audience: nine-month revenue grew 0.50%, OEM and National revenue fell 11.18% while Dealer revenue grew 2.11%, and average monthly unique visitors fell 3% in the third quarter. If the cost savings are exhausted and these trends continue, EBITDA could slip back towards its FY2025 level, which would return leverage to the year-end 2025 ratio and make the 2028 refinancing less comfortable. The issuer's reported Total Net Leverage Ratio of 1.77x is lower than the calculated 2.33x, so the lenders' own measure is the more favourable one; this report relies on the calculated measure because the agreement is not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 10, 19, 26; calculation OE1; calculation DL1; calculation RT14
### Cash flow and capital allocation

Operating cash flow was USD 151.784 million over the last twelve months and free cash flow USD 128.547 million after capital expenditure, which is 79.34% of EBITDA; capital expenditure is only 3.20% of revenue, so most EBITDA reaches cash after interest and tax. In the first nine months of 2026 the company spent USD 74.331 million on share repurchases, 76.39% of free cash flow, repaid USD 10.0 million of the revolving loan and paid the final USD 10.9 million D2C Media earnout in April 2026. Repurchases are discretionary and USD 100.2 million of the programme remains, so a weaker year would let management redirect cash to debt, and the same discretion lets management accelerate returns instead.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 10, 26; calculation LC1; calculation LX1; calculation FC1; calculation FC2; calculation FC3; calculation CX1

Cash is seasonal. It fell to USD 33.287 million at 30 June 2026 after payments of accrued compensation (the line fell from USD 38.074 million at year-end 2025 to USD 15.238 million), the May coupon and repurchases, which lifted net leverage to 2.64x at that date before it returned to 2.33x at 30 September. Net leverage at interim quarter-ends therefore needs care when compared across dates.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_cars_cars-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation ND4; calculation RT11; calculation RT14
### Liquidity and maturity profile

Liquidity was USD 369.553 million at 30 September 2026: cash of USD 64.553 million plus USD 305.0 million undrawn under the USD 350.0 million revolving loan due in 2029, with no letter of credit printed against it. No debt matures until the USD 400.0 million notes fall due in November 2028, which are 89.89% of principal, so refinancing that single payment, not near-term liquidity, is the main event risk. The notes' coupon costs USD 25.5 million a year, and the filings put the debt's fair value at USD 427.3 million against USD 445.0 million of principal, which indicates the market values it below par but gives no price or yield.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9, 25; calculation LQ1; calculation RV1; calculation NT1; calculation CP1
### Data quality and definitions

Three definitions shape every ratio in this report. EBITDA is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization because the filings print none; debt is balance-sheet carrying value, USD 2.566 million below principal at 30 September 2026; and interest cover uses cash interest paid, which is uneven by quarter because the notes pay on 1 May and 1 November. Fourth-quarter 2025 is derived, not reported, and the 2025 annual report recast the 2024 and 2023 expense lines between functions without changing totals. None of these changes the direction of the leverage trend, but each limits comparison with the issuer's covenant ratios, which are quoted only as printed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9, 25; 10-K_2024-12-31_cars_cars-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 63–64; calculation RC1; calculation Q41

## Gaps

- No adjusted EBITDA or add-back schedule is printed in any of the five filings, so adjusted leverage, adjusted coverage and the adjusted EBITDA bridge are not stated; the filings name adjusted EBITDA only as a performance-share target. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the earnings release or investor presentation that reconciles it.

- Reported EBITDA is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization for every period because no filing prints EBITDA, and it may differ from the credit-agreement measure. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the agreement's definition.

- The credit agreement is not supplied, so the issuer's Senior Secured Net Leverage Ratio, Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio and Total Net Leverage Ratio cannot be recomputed and covenant headroom is not calculated. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement and a compliance certificate.

- The second-quarter report dates the Total Net Leverage Ratio of 1.95x as 30 June 2026 in the debt note and 31 March 2026 in the discussion, while the first-quarter report prints 1.84x for 31 March 2026; neither date is chosen here. Severity: Low. Action: confirm against the compliance certificate.

- The 2025 annual report prints no covenant ratio values at 31 December 2025, so the covenant trend has no year-end 2025 point; the 2024 annual report printed 0.04x and 6.5x for 31 December 2024. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the year-end compliance figures.

- Fourth quarter 2025 is not printed as a quarter; revenue, EBITDA and operating cash flow are derived as the fiscal year less nine months and labelled calculated, and other lines are not derived. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the credit metrics.

- Printed dashes in the cash flow statement and balance sheet, such as acquisitions in the first quarter of 2026 or the current portion of debt, are carried as not supplied and never as zero, and lines that exist in some filings and not others, such as the convertible note purchase, are marked as absent from that filing's statement. Severity: Low. Action: none, because none of these cells is an operand of a ratio.

- Interest income is not disclosed separately from interest expense, net, so the gross interest cost cannot be separated and cover uses cash interest paid. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the cover ratio.
- Gross profit is not presented and the issuer's cost of revenue and operations line is not a complete cost of sales, so no gross margin is stated. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not split; total capital expenditure is capitalised internally developed technology plus purchase of property and equipment. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for free cash flow.
- Funds from operations is not printed and the method gives no formula, so ratios based on it are not calculable. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- Debt carrying values by instrument are not disclosed, so the financing cost adjustment of USD 2.566 million at 30 September 2026 is derived as principal less the balance-sheet carrying value; part of the issuance costs is held as a deferred asset, so the adjustment is not the total cost. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- Security, ranking and guarantors rest on the annual report's lien wording for the debt agreements and on the instrument titles, and the quarterly reports omit that wording; the indenture and credit agreement are not supplied. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain both documents.

- The revolving loan margin, the reference rate now in force and any commitment fee are not stated; the rate of 6.1% in effect at 30 September 2026 is the only rate figure. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement pricing grid.
- Per-share, share-count and comprehensive income lines are not carried in the statement tables because they do not enter any credit metric. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- No balance after 30 September 2026 is supplied. The notes pay interest on 1 May and 1 November, so the 1 November 2026 payment falls after the balance-sheet date and is not reflected. Severity: Low. Action: add post-quarter balances if they become available.

- Credit metrics for FY2023 are not shown because the 2024 annual report prints no 31 December 2023 debt composition or revolver availability; the FY2023 statements are carried in the statement tables only. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- First-half 2025 operating income is printed as 21,705 thousand while the two printed quarters sum to 21,706 thousand, a one-thousand rounding difference in the filing; the printed figures are kept. Severity: Low. Action: none.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Cars.com has no sponsor or controlling holder in the supplied filings, so the creditor question is how the board allocates cash, and the record shows buybacks of USD 159.6 million since the start of 2025 against only USD 15.0 million of debt repaid. Credit risk is moderate and steady while earnings hold, but policy favours shareholders over deleveraging.
Basis: calculation BB1; calculation DP1; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

The operating base is recurring and spread across many dealers, but the audience and OEM media revenue are shrinking, so the 2026 earnings gain rests on cost cuts. A different chief executive signed the 2025 annual report and an 11% workforce reduction followed, which adds execution risk ahead of the November 2028 notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98–99; calculation OE1
### Key findings

Customer risk is low and revenue is recurring. About 80% of revenue comes from subscription solutions, Dealer revenue is 90% of the total and no customer exceeded 10% of revenue in any of the last three years, so cash flow is visible and no single customer loss is a credit event.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 24

Capital allocation favours shareholders over creditors. Buybacks of USD 159.6 million since the start of 2025 are more than ten times the USD 15.0 million of principal repaid, they took 76.39% of free cash flow in the first nine months of 2026, and USD 100.2 million of the programme remains; the company pays no dividend and funds buybacks mainly from operating cash flow.
Basis: calculation BB1; calculation DP1; calculation BB2; calculation FC4; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 26

Governance is conventional and creditor-neutral. There is a separate non-executive chairman, charter defences against takeovers and no named controlling holder, but board independence, holders above any threshold and executive pay are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 95, 99

Management change raises execution risk. A different chief executive signed the 2025 annual report than the 2024 one, an 11% workforce reduction cost USD 8.5 million in March 2026, and a further executive offer letter dated September 2026 gives no role, so policy continuity on buybacks and leverage is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_cars_cars-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98–99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 19, 30

Acquisitions are small and mostly cash-funded, but one contingent claim is open. DealerClub cost USD 25.3 million in cash in January 2025, with up to USD 88.0 million more payable through 2028 in cash or shares, none of it expensed to date; settled in cash it would compete with debt repayment.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 26

The audience is the operating risk to watch. Average monthly unique visitors fell 10% and traffic 7% over nine months, dealer customers slipped 1% year on year and OEM and National revenue fell 11.18%, while revenue per dealer rose 3%, so price and mix rather than volume carry Dealer revenue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 22, 24; calculation OE1

Disclosure is good for monitoring but thin on lender terms. Audited statements, quarterly covenant ratios and a stated compliance position are available, while the debt documents, compliance certificates and proxy statement are not, so willingness evidence can be read but legal capacity cannot.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 61–63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 26
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a moderate, steady view is the pace of shareholder returns: buybacks took 76.39% of nine-month free cash flow, USD 100.2 million of the programme remains and USD 305.0 million of the revolving loan is undrawn, so management could fund further repurchases or the DealerClub earnout with debt, with no sponsor involved. The view would worsen if repurchases were funded by revolver borrowings, if the earnout were paid in cash or if the audience decline reached Dealer revenue; it would improve if repurchases slowed in favour of repayment or the notes were refinanced early. Against that, debt principal fell through 2026, no dividend or debt-funded buyback is documented, and liquidity is ample.
Basis: calculation FC4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 26
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, holders above any threshold and executive pay are not established; the conclusion that no sponsor or controlling holder exists rests on their absence from the filings and would change if a large holder were disclosed.

- The credit agreement and indenture are not supplied, so capacity for restricted payments, debt and liens is not established; the conclusion that buybacks are a policy choice rather than a covenant-bound limit cannot be tested.
- The roles under the December 2025 letter agreement and the September 2026 offer letter are not stated, so the conclusion on leadership change rests only on the change of chief executive signatory.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30
- The settlement mode and likelihood of the DealerClub performance consideration are not stated, so the size of the possible cash call is a ceiling and not an estimate.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8

spans.text: # Cars.com Inc. (cars-1683606): fundamental credit
## Request

Fundamental credit assessment of Cars.com Inc. (cars-1683606), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and financial profile, strengths and weaknesses, downside, ranked drivers and monitoring triggers, from the five supplied annual and quarterly filings and the three earlier modules.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_cars_cars-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2024 | 2025-02-27 | 29ec913f9aba8f8ee6806465185b8e497359f6f3333cd9243bf528ec696f42fe | FY2024 comparison, debt history, 2022 repurchase programme and the earlier chief executive signatory. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025 | 2026-02-26 | 6c0dc82761eff68f6b94ce71138107d711ed6a82147d512dde3f8bdcc4c75ca9 | Business model, competition, risk factors, subscription terms, debt guarantees and covenants, year-end 2025 comparison. |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_cars_cars-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-05-07 | 3a4344399cc4663d9641d8ae6c6fd94c56eca0d4b5369ad96a4e540f91da6bb2 | First-quarter statements used to build the nine-month and last-twelve-months figures. |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_cars_cars-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 | 2026-08-06 | e57c8c4207cd0a76320e6e01813c08d37eb36b363c17e098aab8e1ac6b51d89a | 30 June 2026 balance sheet and the interim cash and net leverage peak. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 | 2026-11-05 | 59760f8792c8eae53d42d00a7dc705e4617f484a5de72e1c93aaafd641a0b442 | Latest statements, debt note, covenant ratios, repurchase programme, earnouts and operating metrics. |
| Module | Name | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | Source readiness | 17142d795f3e64b9aaae6cf2d6803983ede07492de5804d8adc07b81886738ad | Confirms which financing and governance documents are not supplied. |
| CP-1 | Financial foundation | 4a556b7e9de6cb0033bf1259ae5574330462f8ae2030221855294e56c1e0baf6 | Statements, calculated EBITDA, leverage, cover, free cash flow, liquidity and maturity profile. |
| CP-1A | Business & governance | d10cdb6d74fdf70a2ae8a207e13593aa73e597cf81ba7dde22c6c598b326d972 | Ownership, governance, capital allocation and business-model findings. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Cars.com is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative issuer whose creditors are well covered until the USD 400.0 million notes fall due in November 2028, so the risk is a reversal of the 2026 cost-led earnings gain while management returns most free cash flow to shareholders.
Basis: calculation LV1; calculation NT1; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Carrying-value debt is 2.73x last-twelve-months EBITDA, interest is covered 5.67x and free cash flow is 79.34% of EBITDA, but revenue is flat, visitors and OEM media are shrinking and repurchases have been 10.64x the debt repaid since the start of 2025. If EBITDA fell back to its FY2025 level, leverage would be 2.91x with the notes still to be refinanced.
Basis: calculation LV1; calculation CV1; calculation FC2; calculation BB2; calculation DS2; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Key findings

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the strongest support. Nothing falls due before November 2028, USD 305.0 million of the USD 350.0 million revolving loan is undrawn, and cash plus that availability equals 0.84x carrying-value debt, so near-term liquidity does not depend on the capital markets.
Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation LQ2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 25

Leverage is moderate and improving, but the improvement is earnings-led and rests on a calculated EBITDA. Carrying-value debt fell from 2.97x EBITDA at FY2025 to 2.73x, net leverage is 2.33x and interest cover is 5.67x; 72.76% of the nine-month EBITDA gain came from lower cash operating costs while revenue grew only 0.50%, so the gain is easier to reverse than a revenue-led one.
Basis: calculation LV1; calculation LV2; calculation LV3; calculation CV1; calculation EG2; calculation RV1; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cash conversion is high and capital needs are small, which is what supports debt service. Free cash flow was 79.34% of EBITDA and capital expenditure only 3.20% of revenue over the last twelve months, and free cash flow has been steady across the three periods shown; the 11% workforce reduction shows cost flexibility but also that a major cost lever has been used.
Basis: calculation FC2; calculation FC3; calculation CX1; calculation CO1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Shareholder returns, not creditors, set the pace of deleveraging. Repurchases of USD 159.6 million since the start of 2025 are 10.64x the USD 15.0 million of debt repaid and took 76.39% of free cash flow in the first nine months of 2026; USD 100.2 million of the programme remains and it may be suspended at any time, so the policy is reversible, and while the debt agreements restrict distributions in general terms, their limits are not seen and nothing disclosed holds it back.
Basis: calculation BB1; calculation DP1; calculation BB2; calculation BP1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 26; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Revenue is recurring but short-dated, and its growth engine is weakening. About 80% of revenue is subscription-based and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, yet packages are generally renewed month to month, so visibility rests on dealer behaviour and not on contracts; visitors fell 10% and traffic 7% in nine months, dealer customers slipped 1% and OEM and National revenue fell 11.18%, while a 3% rise in revenue per dealer lifted Dealer revenue 2.11%.
Basis: calculation OE1; calculation DL1; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 58, 91; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19, 21

The single large maturity, not near-term liquidity, is the event risk. The USD 400.0 million notes are 89.89% of principal and equal 3.11x last-twelve-months free cash flow, and the fair value of debt is 96.02% of principal against 99.80% at the end of 2025, a discount that may reflect higher market yields or more perceived risk than the leverage ratios imply; the notes' own price and yield are not stated.
Basis: calculation NT1; calculation NT2; calculation FV1; calculation FV2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9

Reported covenant compliance is favourable but cannot be verified here. The issuer reports interest coverage of 7.33x against a floor of 3.0x and a senior secured net leverage ratio that is negative against a ceiling of 3.5x, and its Total Net Leverage Ratio of 1.77x is 0.56x below the 2.33x calculated here; the definitions sit in the credit agreement, which is not supplied, so headroom is not calculated.
Basis: calculation CV3; calculation LV6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

Governance adds execution risk but no sponsor risk. No sponsor or controlling holder is named and the chairman is separate from the chief executive, while the chief executive who signed the 2025 annual report differs from the 2024 signatory and an 11% workforce reduction cost USD 8.5 million in March 2026, so continuity of buyback and leverage policy is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that earnings, cash flow and the balance sheet have moved the right way together: leverage fell from 2.97x to 2.73x, free cash flow stayed steady and USD 305.0 million of the revolving loan is undrawn, while management attributes the audience decline to a deliberate shift towards high-intent shoppers and revenue per dealer rose 3%. If that account holds, the 2026 cost savings are a lasting margin gain and the 2028 notes can be refinanced from a lower leverage base. The strongest evidence against a comfortable reading is that debt is valued at 96.02% of principal against 99.80% at the end of 2025, with flat revenue and month-to-month dealer subscriptions behind it. The view would improve if dealer customers and revenue per dealer rose together for two quarters while repurchases slowed in favour of repayment or the notes were refinanced early, and it would worsen if EBITDA fell back to its FY2025 level, which would take leverage to 2.91x, if repurchases were funded from the revolving loan or if dealer customers fell by more than the 1% seen now.

Basis: calculation LV1; calculation LV3; calculation DS2; calculation FV1; calculation FV2; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21
### Limitations

- EBITDA is calculated from operating income plus depreciation and amortization, so the moderate-leverage conclusion rests on a measure the issuer does not state; its own Total Net Leverage Ratio of 1.77x is below the 2.33x calculated here, and the conclusion would move towards that lower figure if the credit agreement's definitions were applied.
Basis: calculation LV2; calculation LV6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- No credit rating, bond price, yield or peer data are supplied, so moderate leverage is an absolute judgement and the signal in the fair value of debt cannot be tested against peers or against the notes' own trading level.
Basis: calculation FV1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9

- The conditions for drawing the revolving loan and its exact 2029 maturity month are not stated, so the conclusion that undrawn availability backstops the 2028 notes would weaken if drawing were restricted or the facility fell due earlier than the notes' refinancing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 25

- Audience figures are management-defined, are measured on one analytics platform and exclude traffic to three of the company's other websites, so the conclusion that the audience is shrinking would be overstated if the excluded traffic is growing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

- The downside is an arithmetic test on reported figures because no management projection or guidance is supplied, so the conclusion that EBITDA could return to its FY2025 level is a sensitivity and not a forecast.
Basis: calculation DS1; calculation DS2
### Upstream values used

All five filings and the three earlier modules were available, so the module is a full run. The balances, last-twelve-months EBITDA, interest cover, free cash flow and liquidity come from Financial foundation and are restated in the calculations with their inputs; the ownership, governance and capital-allocation findings come from Business & governance. Source readiness confirms that the credit agreement, the indenture and the proxy statement are not among the supplied documents. Financial foundation found no event after 30 September 2026 that adjusts net debt, so no pro forma figure is shown.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Company description and ownership

Cars.com runs an online automotive marketplace with dealer websites, trade and appraisal tools and media products. About 80% of revenue is subscription-based and Dealer revenue is 90.36% of the nine-month 2026 total, so recurring dealer billing supports cash-flow visibility and debt service, while the OEM and National media line and the audience that feeds every product are the exposed parts.
Basis: calculation MX1; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2

Cars.com is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling holder named, a chairman separate from the chief executive and charter provisions that can discourage a takeover. Creditor alignment therefore depends on board policy and not on an owner's willingness to support the company, and no such support is assumed. The notes are titled senior unsecured and the annual report states that the guarantors granted liens on substantially all of their assets for the debt agreements, so legal ranking is not verified here.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 83
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is predictable in pattern but no longer grows on volume. Nine-month 2026 revenue grew 0.50%, Dealer revenue grew 2.11% on a 3% rise in revenue per dealer from higher-tier marketplace packages, dealer customers fell 1% and OEM and National revenue fell 11.18%. Packages are generally renewed month to month, so a dealer that sees fewer leads can leave quickly, and Dealer revenue, 90.36% of the total, would show that in EBITDA first. Management attributes the 10% fall in unique visitors to a deliberate shift towards high-intent shoppers; the filings report no total lead volume or retention rate, so the claim is not tested.
Basis: calculation RV1; calculation DL1; calculation OE1; calculation MX1; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19–22
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are mainly people, marketing and technology, and management has shown it can cut them: cash operating costs fell 1.70% in nine months 2026, which delivered 72.76% of the EBITDA gain, after an 11% workforce reduction that cost USD 8.5 million in March 2026. EBITDA margin was 22.34% in FY2024, 21.03% in FY2025 and 22.32% over the last twelve months, so margin has recovered to its FY2024 level on flat revenue. Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure through further cost action, but a major lever has been used and a revenue decline would meet a smaller cushion; the filings do not split fixed from variable costs.
Basis: calculation CO1; calculation EG2; calculation MG1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 19
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital needs are small: capital expenditure is 3.20% of revenue and the filings do not split maintenance from growth spending. Free cash flow was USD 128.143 million in FY2024, USD 125.734 million in FY2025 and USD 128.547 million over the last twelve months, 79.34% of EBITDA and 2.24% above FY2025, after cash interest of USD 28.553 million. Cash is seasonal inside the year: it fell to USD 33.287 million at 30 June 2026 after bonus payments, the May coupon and repurchases, before recovering to USD 64.553 million at 30 September 2026.

Basis: calculation FC1; calculation FC2; calculation FC3; calculation CX1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cars_cars-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4–5; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is high and the contest is for audience: the direct competitors named are CarGurus, AutoTrader and TrueCar, dealer software providers such as Cox Automotive compete for dealer budgets, and search engines, social platforms and generative AI chat engines compete for the same shoppers. Substitutes matter most through AI answer engines that can give vehicle information without sending shoppers to Cars.com, which would cut organic traffic and the value of a dealer subscription. Dealer buyer power is limited because no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, but OEM and National customers are few and can change media strategy independent of the product, which explains the volatility of that line. Search engines and app stores hold the most supplier power because most traffic arrives organically and ranking changes can lower visits.
### Macro and technology factors

Technology is the factor that changes the credit view: AI answer engines and search changes could lower traffic and lead volumes, and the issuer lists them among its risks. Economic factors act through vehicle sales volumes, affordability, tariffs and interest rates, which the issuer says influence OEM and dealer marketing spend; the floating-rate revolving loan is 10.11% of principal, so direct interest-rate exposure is small. Regulatory and political factors are not presented as a primary credit driver in the supplied filings.
Basis: calculation FL1; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19, 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are average: the issuer describes industry-leading brand recognition, but revenue of USD 725.943 million over the last twelve months cannot be ranked because no market share or peer data are supplied. Competitive advantage is average: brand and audience scale support pricing, but traffic is falling and search and AI platforms can intermediate. Business diversification is average: dealers are many and none exceeds 10% of revenue, but Dealer revenue is 90.36% of the total. Cost and capex flexibility is strong: capital expenditure is 3.20% of revenue and cash costs fell 1.70% in nine months. Margin stability is average: margin moved 1.31 percentage points between FY2024 and FY2025 and recovered through cost cuts. Free cash flow stability is strong: free cash flow stayed between USD 125.734 million and USD 128.547 million across three periods. Ability to refinance is average: the notes are 89.89% of principal and the fair value of debt is 96.02% of principal. Liquidity is strong: it equals 0.84x carrying-value debt with no maturity before November 2028. Financial policy and governance are weak from a creditor's view: repurchases are 10.64x debt repaid and the debt agreements are not seen. Credit supports are liquidity, cash conversion and recurring dealer revenue; constraints are the audience, the bullet maturity and shareholder-first policy; the trend in leverage is down; the missing data are the debt documents, peer data and any management projection.
Basis: calculation LQ2; calculation FC1; calculation CX1; calculation MG1; calculation NT1; calculation FV1; calculation BB2; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to 24 months the supports are the remaining annualisation of the March 2026 cost reduction, price and mix gains from higher-tier packages, a fixed coupon of USD 25.500 million on the notes and no maturity; the pressures are the audience decline, the 1% fall in dealer customers, OEM media weakness and the DealerClub earnout of up to USD 88.0 million, which may be paid in cash or in stock if mutually agreed through 2028 and has not been expensed to date. Over three to five years the central event is the November 2028 refinancing of USD 400.0 million, priced on the leverage and growth then shown, with the shift of search towards AI as the structural headwind to audience and dealer value. The sector factors the issuer names are vehicle sales volumes, affordability, tariffs, interest rates and electric vehicle adoption.
Basis: calculation CP1; calculation NT1; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21, 26
### Downside scenario

The most plausible downside is audience-led. Search and AI platforms divert organic traffic and unique visitors keep falling beyond the 10% seen in nine months 2026; the first operational break is at the dealer, where higher-tier package adoption stalls, dealer customers fall faster than the 1% now seen and Dealer revenue, 90.36% of the total, stops growing while OEM and National revenue keeps falling. With the March 2026 cost reduction already taken, little cost cushion is left, so EBITDA drifts back towards its FY2025 level, 6.13% below the last twelve months. At that level carrying-value debt is 2.91x EBITDA, net debt 2.48x and cash interest cover 5.33x, so the transmission is moderate leverage rising from 2.73x and not a covenant event. Liquidity holds: free cash flow at the FY2025 level of USD 125.734 million still funds interest and capital expenditure, and USD 305.0 million of the revolving loan is undrawn. The pressure arrives at refinancing: even if all free cash flow and cash were kept for the 25 months to October 2028, USD 67.641 million of the USD 400.0 million notes would still need other funding, and any repurchases add to that gap. Management's levers are to suspend the repurchase programme, cut costs again, settle the DealerClub earnout in stock where agreed or draw the revolving loan. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; whether the notes can be refinanced on acceptable terms against a weaker audience is the open question, and the signals to watch are in the monitoring triggers.
Basis: calculation DS1; calculation DS2; calculation DS3; calculation DS4; calculation RP1; calculation FC1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 26
### Overall credit view

Overall, Cars.com presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring dealer subscriptions, low customer concentration and small capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking audience, a cost-led earnings recovery and a shareholder-first financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow has been steady across three periods and converts 79.34% of EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA holding near its current level, the revolving loan staying available and repurchases slowing before the November 2028 maturity. The primary downside path is audience erosion that reaches Dealer revenue. A more definitive opinion would require the credit agreement and indenture, the proxy statement, the issuer's reconciliation of EBITDA, and peer and market-price data.
Basis: calculation FC2; calculation LV1; calculation NT1; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths are ranked from the most to the least important for creditors.

The first strength is liquidity with no near-term maturity: nothing falls due before November 2028 and USD 305.0 million of the revolving loan is undrawn, so interest, capital expenditure and repurchases are funded from operations and a backstop exists if the capital markets are shut. That lowers near-term default probability and gives time to refinance.
Basis: calculation LQ1; calculation LQ2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 25

The second is cash conversion: free cash flow is 79.34% of EBITDA on capital expenditure of 3.20% of revenue, so debt service does not rely on asset sales and the cash is there to repay or refinance the notes.
Basis: calculation FC2; calculation CX1; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The third is recurring dealer revenue with no customer above 10% of revenue, which spreads the loss from any one customer and supports predictable cash receipts, subject to the month-to-month term of the packages.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 58, 91
The fourth is moderate, falling leverage with wide cover: 2.73x carrying-value debt to EBITDA and 5.67x interest cover leave room for a decline in EBITDA before debt service is strained.
Basis: calculation LV1; calculation CV1; Financial foundation (CP-1)
Weaknesses are ranked from the most to the least important for creditors.

The first weakness is a shareholder-first policy: repurchases are 10.64x the debt repaid and 76.39% of nine-month free cash flow, so cash that could cut debt leaves the company and the 2028 notes are left to refinance.
Basis: calculation BB2; calculation BP1; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second is audience and OEM media erosion: visitors are down 10%, dealer customers 1% and OEM and National revenue 11.18%, which weakens the value offered to dealers and advertisers and, if it reaches Dealer revenue, EBITDA and cover.
Basis: calculation OE1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 19

The third is a single bullet maturity: the USD 400.0 million notes are 89.89% of principal and 3.11x annual free cash flow, so they must be refinanced or funded from the revolving loan, and the fair value of debt at 96.02% of principal may reflect market pricing of that risk or higher yields.
Basis: calculation NT1; calculation NT2; calculation FV1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9
The fourth is a cost-led earnings gain: 72.76% of the nine-month EBITDA gain came from lower cash costs, so a return to the FY2025 EBITDA level would take leverage to 2.91x.
Basis: calculation EG2; calculation DS2

The fifth is untested debt terms and leadership change: the covenant ratios are reported as met but the agreements are not seen, and the chief executive signatory changed between the 2024 and 2025 annual reports.
Basis: calculation CV3; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are repaying the revolving loan from retained free cash flow if repurchases slow, an early refinancing of the notes while leverage is at its lowest in the periods shown, and DealerClub growth that earns the earnout from its own cash flow. Threats that could weaken it are AI-led loss of search traffic, the loss of one of the few OEM media buyers and a cash settlement of the DealerClub earnout alongside continued repurchases.
Basis: calculation LV1; 10-K_2025-12-31_cars_cars-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 19, 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cars_cars-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26
